Location controls in the survey year, in one call

Source: R/controls.R
time_varying_controls.Rd

Takes, for each household, the layer of the year that matches its survey: population, night lights, land cover by year. With climate, it adds the climate normals of the years before the survey year. One row per household and survey year.

Usage

time_varying_controls(
  survey,
  layers = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  interview = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  match = c("same_year", "previous_year", "nearest"),
  climate = NULL,
  years = 30,
  stats = c("mean", "sd", "cv"),
  density = TRUE,
  log = "nightlight",
  buffer = 0,
  kind = NULL,
  boundaries = NULL,
  control = controls_control()
)

Arguments

survey

The survey: a data frame with coordinates, a household identifier and interview dates, or a table from prepare_coord(); or a named list of them.

layers

A named list of rasters with one layer per year, dated with terra::time(); e.g. list(pop = worldpop).

lat, lon, id, interview

<tidy-select> Survey columns: coordinates (found by name when left out), household identifier and interview date. Not needed after prepare_coord().

year

<tidy-select> Optional survey column holding the survey year, instead of the interview date.

match

"same_year", "previous_year" or "nearest".

climate

Optional named list of climate rasters (paths or SpatRasters) for the normals, e.g. list(pre = chirps).

years

Number of years before the survey year for the normals.

stats

Statistics of the normals: any of "mean", "sd", "cv", "min", "max", "median", "sum".

density

Add the density of count layers.

log

Names of layers to add as log(1 + value).

buffer

A radius in metres; 0 is the location's own cell.

kind

Optional named character vector of layer kinds: "continuous", "count" or "categorical".

boundaries

Optional administrative divisions: indicators are then computed per cell and averaged per division (area shares).

control

Further options, see extremes_control().

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per household and survey year.

Details

match decides which yearly layer serves a survey year: the same year, the previous one (to use only data from before the interview) or the nearest available. The year used is kept in <layer>_year, and the labels say which rule was applied. Count layers (population) also get <layer>_density, per square kilometre of the cells summed; layers named in log get log_<layer>, the log of one plus the value.

The normals use calc_par() on the series from years years before the survey year to the end of the year before it; when the data cover fewer years, a message says which.

See also

static_controls(), calc_par()

Examples

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)
template <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif",
                                    package = "c4e"))[[1]]
pop <- terra::rast(template, nlyrs = 3, vals = rep(c(100, 200, 300), each = 36))
terra::time(pop) <- as.Date(c("2021-01-01", "2022-01-01", "2023-01-01"))

time_varying_controls(survey, list(pop = pop), id = hhid,
                      interview = interview, match = "previous_year")
#> Using lat as `lat`.
#> Using lon as `lon`.
#> Taking the coordinates as longitude and latitude in "EPSG:4326"; give `crs`
#> otherwise.
